mode_rationale: The source is additive and greenfield in intent ('se me ocurre... crear'), with the only negation aimed at an external system (Hooba has no API). No defect is reported. However research surfaced one latent defect (C2) that is a hard prerequisite, giving this an investigation-flavoured sub-thread inside an enrichment proposal.
summary_oneline: Compose a Hooba browser-automation agent on the existing scraping DSL, reachable over Telegram/WhatsApp, with a gestoria wiki plane mirrored to Obsidian
summary: The request is to automate a Spanish legally-mandated, API-less accounting SaaS (Hooba) through the browser, and to drive that automation conversationally from Telegram/WhatsApp with a durable wiki+Obsidian memory. Research shows the proposal is substantially better-supported than the source assumes: the JSON action DSL already exists as 27 typed BrowserAction Pydantic models (C1) including Authenticate, AwaitHuman, UploadFile and WaitForDownload; FEAT-222 already merged parameterized TemplatePlan binding, a session-affine ScrapingFlow DAG and a resumable FlowExecutor (C3); both drivers and a Chrome DevTools MCP WebAgent are live (C4); the wiki tools, ObsidianToolkit, Telegram/WhatsApp wrappers, credential broker with signed audit ledger, Excel loaders and an APScheduler-based scheduler all exist (C6, C7, C8, C10). The genuinely new work is therefore much narrower than 'build a BrowserAutomationToolkit': close the eight actions that executor.py silently stubs with return True (C2), validate plan steps at rest (C12), build a Hooba-specific domain toolkit over TemplatePlan/ScrapingFlow, add Google Calendar event tools (C9), and stand up a gestoria wiki plane — the last of which should follow rather than race FEAT-452 (C11).

constraints.title: Eight DSL actions are stubbed, not missing
constraints.detail: executor.py:298-311 returns True for authenticate, upload_file, wait_for_download, get_cookies, set_cookies, await_human, await_keypress, await_browser_event. A Hooba plan whose first step is authenticate proceeds believing it is logged in, operating subsequent steps against a login page.
constraints.implication: Closing this gap is a prerequisite task, not an enhancement. Silent success against an accounting system is worse than failure.

constraints.title: FEAT-222 already fixed this defect class once, partially
constraints.detail: FEAT-222 spec §1 gap 4 identified exactly this stub pattern for Loop/Conditional and extracted them into advanced_actions.py. The remaining eight were left behind.
constraints.implication: advanced_actions.py is the established extraction pattern to follow; do not invent a new one.

constraints.title: Plan steps are untyped at rest
constraints.detail: ScrapingPlan.steps is List[Dict[str, Any]]; typed BrowserAction parsing happens only at execution time in the legacy tool.
constraints.implication: Malformed plans fail mid-transaction. For financial writes, validate the whole plan against the BrowserAction union before opening the browser.

constraints.title: AgentsFlow is not an AbstractBot
constraints.detail: AgentsFlow(PersistenceMixin); AgentTool.__init__ requires an AbstractBot. as_tool() cannot wrap a flow.
constraints.implication: The Excel expense pipeline must go through ExecutionPlanToolkit.plan_execute (bounded, LLM-free, with run_id polling) rather than a hypothetical AgentsFlow.as_tool().

constraints.title: Scheduling lives in ai-parrot-server
constraints.detail: parrot/scheduler/manager.py and BaseSchedulerCallback are in the server distribution, not core.
constraints.implication: Tax-deadline reminders imply deploying ai-parrot-server, not just running a bot process. That is a deployment decision the source has not made.

constraints.title: Google Calendar has scopes but no tools
constraints.detail: GoogleClient declares calendar scopes and returns a service config dict; nothing consumes it. O365 has real event tools with per-user OAuth.
constraints.implication: Google Calendar event tooling is net-new and self-contained — a clean candidate for deferral out of a first release.

constraints.title: FEAT-452 owns the domain-plane + vault-mirror pattern and is in flight
constraints.detail: All six FEAT-452 tasks are in-progress on dev, building a separate notes wiki plane, registering it as a queryable namespace, scoping nightly vault ingest to a folder, and adding telegram_chat_scope.
constraints.implication: FEAT-453's wiki layer must consume that mechanism, not race it. Two incompatible domain-plane designs in one repo is the failure mode to avoid.

constraints.title: Channel authorization is a financial control here
constraints.detail: WhatsAppAgentWrapper._is_authorized(wa_id) and telegram/auth.py gate who can talk to the bot.
constraints.implication: This agent can spend money and file tax-relevant records; the allowlist is a security boundary, and await_human before any legally-effective write should be the default posture.

constraints.title: Fan-out on a shared authenticated session is known deferred debt
constraints.detail: FEAT-222 lists this as an explicit non-goal, safe in sequential mode only.
constraints.implication: Fine for a single autonomo, but the expense-import flow must stay sequential over one Hooba session.

what_changes.change: Replace the 8-action stub branch with real dispatch, extracting the implementations out of tool.py following the advanced_actions.py pattern
Delegate authenticate/await_human/upload_file/wait_for_download/cookies to the extracted module, eliminating the duplicate implementation
Add opt-in validation of steps against the BrowserAction union at load time

Building a WikiToolkit or ObsidianToolkit — both exist and are complete (C6)
Building WhatsApp or Telegram transport — both ship, WhatsApp with two transports (C7)
Building scheduling machinery — only a new callback is needed (C8)
Re-implementing the domain wiki plane / vault mirror pattern that FEAT-452 is landing (C11)
Concurrent fan-out over one authenticated Hooba session — FEAT-222 deferred debt (C3)

FEAT-207 shared-state toolkit: one AbstractToolkit instance initialized with live dependencies, shared across every tool call (as ExecutionPlanToolkit and the skill toolkits do)

overall_confidence_reasoning: Localization and component-existence claims are uniformly high-confidence and directly read from source. Confidence is held at medium by three things, none of which more research on this repo would fix: the scope claim C13 is an inference over a union of findings rather than a verified inventory; the decisive feasibility question C14 is external to the codebase; and the feature as stated spans three or four deliverables, so any single-spec scope statement is provisional until U4 is answered.

recommended_next_command.rationale: The highest-value slice — closing the eight stubbed actions, validating plans at load, and building the Hooba domain toolkit on TemplatePlan/ScrapingFlow — is high-confidence, precisely localized, and blocking everything else. Spec that first under FEAT-453 and give the conversational agent, the gestoria wiki plane and the calendar/reminder work their own FEAT-IDs.
